It is a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of (yu'minu), and it is in the plural by considering the meaning, after having been in the singular first by considering the wording. It is said: it is a hal from the pronoun in (ilayhim), and this is closer only in wording. The circumstantial clause was brought as an allusion to the hypocrites, who believe out of fear of being killed. (Lillah), "for God," is connected to (khashi'in). It is said: it is connected to the verb negated after it, and it is in the sense of being placed later, as if He, glorified is He, had said: ﴿They do not sell the signs of God for a small price﴾ for the sake of God, the Exalted. The first is preferable. In this negation there is an explicit statement of their opposition to the distorters. The clause is also in the position of a circumstantial clause. The meaning is that they do not take a small return for distorting the Book and concealing the truth, such as bribes and food, as those described by Him, glorified is He, earlier have done. The description of the price as "small" is either because everything taken for distortion is like that, even if it fills the East and the West, or merely as an allusion to those who take it, and praise of them by what has been mentioned, not only because they do not take it, but because this includes the manifestation of the guidance in the verses and the proofs of his prophethood (peace and blessings of God be upon him and his family).

﴿Those﴾, that is, those described with the praiseworthy characteristics mentioned. The choice of the distant demonstrative form indicates the loftiness of their rank and the remoteness of their station in nobility and excellence. ﴿For them is their reward with their Lord﴾, that is, the reward of their deeds and the recompense of their obedience. The idafa (possessive construction) is for definiteness (al-'ahd), meaning the reward specifically belonging to them, promised to them in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Those will be given their reward twice﴾, and His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He will give you two portions of His mercy﴾. In expressing it with the title of lordship (al-rububiyyah) together with the attribution to their pronoun, there is a subtlety that is not hidden. In the sentence there are several possibilities of grammatical analysis (i'rab). They have said: ﴿Those﴾ is a subject (mubtada') and the adverbial phrase is its predicate (khabar), and ﴿their reward﴾ is raised by the adverbial phrase. Or the adverbial phrase is a fronted predicate (khabar muqaddam), and ﴿their reward﴾ is a delayed subject (mubtada' mu'akhkhar), and the clause is the predicate of the subject. ﴿With their Lord﴾ is in the accusative as a circumstantial (hal) from ﴿their reward﴾. It is said: it is connected to it, on the basis that the implied sense is "for them is to be rewarded with their Lord." It is also permitted that ﴿their reward﴾ is a subject and ﴿with their Lord﴾ is its predicate, and ﴿for them﴾ is connected to what the sentence implies of settledness and establishment, because it has the status of an adverbial phrase. The most correct of these possibilities is the one commonly used by the grammarians.

﴿Indeed, God is swift in reckoning﴾ (199). It is either a metaphor (kinayah) for the perfection of His knowledge, Exalted is He, of the measures of rewards and the levels of deservingness, and that He gives each doer his due in the proper manner and measure. In that case the clause is a new sentence coming by way of causal explanation (ta'lil) for His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿For them is their reward with their Lord﴾, or a concluding addition (tadhyil) explaining the reason for the ruling conveyed by what has been mentioned. Or it is a metaphor for the nearness of the promised reward, since the swiftness of reckoning requires the swiftness of recompense. In that case the clause is a completion (takmil) of what precedes it, for it has the meaning of a promise, as if it were said: "For them is a reward with their Lord" soon. It has been separated (from what precedes it) because the ruling of the nearness of the reward is something that confirms its establishment. Then, when He, glorified is He, explained within the folds of this noble surah...

**Commentary of al-Alusi (Ruh al-Ma'ani) on surah 3, verse 200 (part 1 of 2):**

Having explained the wisdom and the rulings, described the condition of the believers and the disbelievers, and set out the pains that the noble believers suffered at the hands of those base people, He concluded the surah with that which yields the fragrance of holding fast to what has passed, and which loses the schemes of the enemies by complying with what it contains, even if the wide space were too narrow for them. Thus the Mighty One, the Speaker, said: ﴿O you who believe, be patient﴾, that is, restrain your souls from impatience at what befalls them. The apparent meaning is that the command encompasses the three divisions of patience, which differ in rank, mentioned in the report: patience in the face of calamity, patience in obedience, and patience in refraining from disobedience. ﴿And endure﴾, that is, persevere through the hardships of war with the enemies of Allah, the Exalted, with greater perseverance than theirs. Its mention after the general command to be patient is because it is more severe, and therefore more excellent. So the conjunction is like the conjunction of Gabriel with the angels, and of ﴿the middle prayer﴾ with ﴿the prayers﴾. Although this ultimately leads to a command to jihad, it is more eloquent than that. ﴿And guard the frontiers﴾, that is, remain stationed in the frontier posts, keeping your horses there, holding them in readiness, watching for the raid, preparing for it, and reaching in this the utmost extent, more than your enemies do. Garrisoning (al-murabatah) is also a kind of patience, so the conjunction here is like the preceding conjunction.

The two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related from Sahl ibn Sa'd that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A day of garrisoning in the way of Allah is better than the world and whatever is in it." Ibn Majah related with a sound chain from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever dies while garrisoning in the way of Allah, the reward of the righteous deed he used to do will continue to be credited to him, his provision will continue for him, he will be safe from the tester (al-fattan), and Allah will raise him secure from terror." al-Tabarani related with an acceptable chain from Jabir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever garrisons for a day in the way of Allah, Allah will place between him and the Fire seven trenches, each trench like the distance of seven heavens and seven earths." Abu al-Shaykh related from Anas, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Prayer in a land of garrisoning is worth a thousand thousand prayers."

It is also reported from Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, that garrisoning is better than jihad, because it preserves the blood of the Muslims, whereas jihad sheds the blood of the polytheists.

﴿And fear Allah﴾ in opposing His command absolutely, so that all that has passed is included in it at the first level of inclusion. ﴿That perhaps you may prosper﴾ (200), that is, so that you may succeed, attain your desire, reach your aim and arrive at success in your quest. That is the true meaning of prosperity (al-falah). This verse, as you have heard, comprises what guides the believer to that which is in the interest of religion and worldly life, and raises him to the highest summit. Some have established this by saying that a person's conditions are of two kinds: the first is what concerns him alone, and the second is what concerns him insofar as he shares with the people of his household and city. Glorified is He, looking to the first, commanded patience, which includes enduring the hardship of reflection and inference in knowing the Oneness (tawhid), prophethood, and the Return; patience in performing obligatory and recommended acts and in avoiding what is forbidden; and patience in the hardships and afflictions and fears of this world. Looking to the second, He commanded perseverance (al-musabarah), which includes bearing the bad characters of relatives and strangers, refraining from retaliating against them, enjoining good and forbidding evil, and striving against the enemies of religion by tongue and by spear. Then, since the imposition on a person of what has been mentioned requires the reform of the psychic faculties that incite to the opposite of that, He commanded garrisoning, in its broadest sense, whether garrisoning of a frontier or of the soul. Then, since attention to the Truth, Majestic and Exalted, is necessary in all deeds and words so that they may be counted, He commanded taqwa. Then, when the duties of servanthood were complete, He concluded the discourse with the duty of lordship, which is the hope of success from Him. Ended.

It is not hidden that, despite what it contains, this has evident strained reasoning and forced interpretation, which none but a stubborn person would deny. More preferable than this is to say: He, Exalted, first commanded the general patience, because, as the report says, it is in the position of the head with respect to the body, and it is the key to relief.

Some have said: everything has a essence (jawhar), the essence of man is intellect, and the essence of intellect is patience. Many have claimed that all lofty ranks and elevated religious and worldly stations are attained only through patience. From here the poet said:

*I shall make the difficult easy, or I shall attain my wish;*
*Hopes are never subdued except for the patient.*

Then He commanded, secondly, a particular kind of patience, which is striving (al-mujahadah), through which comes general benefit and complete honour. It has come from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "If you abandon jihad, Allah will impose upon you a humiliation that He will not remove until you return to your religion." Then the discourse ascends to another kind of this, higher and more precious, which is garrisoning, that is, residing at a frontier to repel an expected harm from those beyond it. Then, at the last of the command, He commanded general taqwa, for without it some of showing-off, self-admiration, and seeing other than Allah, glorified is He, would have mixed with those things and corrupted them. With this the electuary that cures the ailment is complete, and the drink that quenches thirst is clarified.

From here He followed that with His words, Mighty is His affair: ﴿That perhaps you may prosper﴾. This is based on what is well known in the interpretation of the verse, though other transmitted reports differ. Ibn Mardawayh related from Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: Abu Hurayrah turned to me one day and said: "Do you know, nephew, concerning what this verse was revealed: ﴿O you who believe, be patient﴾, etc.?" I said: "No." He said: "Indeed, in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) there was no military campaign in which they garrisoned. Rather, it was revealed concerning a people who frequent the mosques, who pray the prayer at its appointed times and then remember Allah in them. Concerning them it was revealed," that is, ﴿be patient﴾ over the five prayers, ﴿and endure﴾ your souls and your desires, ﴿and garrison﴾ in your mosques, ﴿and fear Allah﴾ regarding what He has taught you, ﴿that perhaps you may prosper﴾."

Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Muslim related from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Shall I not inform you of that by which Allah erases sins and raises ranks? Perfecting the ablution in disliked conditions, many steps to the mosques, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer. That is garrisoning; that is garrisoning; that is garrisoning."

Perhaps this report from Abu Hurayrah is more authentic than the first report, together with the ruling in it that in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) there was no military campaign in which they garrisoned, which is far-fetched, for it hardly can be accepted. Furthermore, this report, though sound, does not contradict the well-known interpretation, since the definite article in "al-ribat" in it may be for a known referent, meaning garrisoning in the way of Allah, and his saying (peace be upon him): "That is garrisoning" is like the expression "Zayd is a lion," intended as an emphatic comparison of that to garrisoning.

'Abd ibn Humayd related from Zayd ibn Aslam that what is meant is: be patient in jihad, endure your enemy, and garrison for your religion. From al-Hasan, he said: be patient in calamity, endure in the prayers, and garrison in jihad in the way of Allah. From Qatadah, he said: be patient in obedience to Allah, endure the people of error, and garrison in the way of Allah. This is close to the first, and the first is preferable.

* * *

This (and from the category of allusion): ﴿Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾, that is, the upper world and the lower world, ﴿and the alternation of night and day﴾, the darkness and the light, ﴿are signs for those of understanding﴾, who are those who look upon creation with the eye of the Truth, ﴿who remember Allah standing﴾ in the station of the Spirit through witnessing, ﴿and sitting﴾ in the place of the heart through unveiling, ﴿and on their sides﴾, that is, their turnings within the recesses of the self through striving. Some have said: ﴿who remember Allah standing﴾, that is, standing in following His commands, ﴿and sitting﴾, that is, sitting away from His prohibitions and forbiddings, ﴿and on their sides﴾, that is, and avoiding the contemplation of transgressions in any state. ﴿And they reflect﴾ with their minds purified of the impurities of illusion ﴿upon the creation of the heavens and the earth﴾. That reflection has two meanings. The first is the seeking of the absence of the hearts in the unseen, which are the treasures of the lights of the attributes, in order to perceive the lights of power that convey the witness to the witnessed. The second is the roaming of the hearts in the manner of reflection

*(page 177)*

in the origination of the dominion, seeking to witness the King in the dominion. When they witness, they say: ﴿Our Lord, You did not create this in vain﴾; rather, it is mirrors of Your names and manifestations of Your attributes. The intent is made clear by the saying of Labid:

*Surely everything other than Allah is vain, and every bliss is surely to pass away.*

﴿Glory be to You﴾, that is, exalting You from there being any existence other than You. ﴿Then protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾, which is the fire of veiling oneself through the created things from seeing the Creator. ﴿Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit to the Fire﴾ and veil from the vision, ﴿You have certainly disgraced him﴾ and humiliated him by distance from You. ﴿And for the wrongdoers﴾, who associated with Him what has no existence in the caravan or in the battle, ﴿there are no helpers﴾, because the overpowering manifestation of the forceful self-disclosure has overcome them.

﴿Our Lord, indeed we heard﴾ with the ears of our hearts ﴿a caller﴾ from our secret depths, which are the right bank of the valley of the Spirit, ﴿calling to faith﴾ of direct vision, ﴿that you believe in your Lord, so we believed﴾, that is, they witnessed your Lord and we witnessed. Or: ﴿indeed we heard﴾ at the first station ﴿a caller calling to faith﴾, and by him is meant Allah, Exalted, when He addressed the spirits in the realm of atoms with His words, glorified is He: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ for that is a call to them to faith. ﴿So we believed﴾, meaning their saying "Yes" when they witnessed Him, glorified is He, there. ﴿Our Lord, forgive us our sins﴾, that is, the sins of our attributes through Your attributes. ﴿And remove from us our evil deeds﴾, that is, the evil of our actions through witnessing Your actions. ﴿And take us﴾ from our essences by a chosen death ﴿with the righteous﴾, and they are those who stand upon the limit of singling out and oneness. ﴿Our Lord, and give us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾, by Your saying: ﴿For those who do good is the best reward and more﴾. ﴿And do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection﴾ by veiling us, through Your blessing, from You. ﴿Indeed You do not fail in promise.﴾ ﴿So their Lord responded to them﴾ out of perfection of His mercy: ﴿Indeed I will not let the work of any worker among you be lost, whether male or female﴾. The heart and its deed are like sincerity and certainty; the soul and its deed, when it abandons struggles and outward acts of obedience, are the female. ﴿Some of you are from others﴾, since one origin unites you, which is the human spirit. ﴿Those who emigrated﴾ from other than Allah, the Exalted, to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, ﴿and were expelled from their homes﴾, which are the beloved things of their selves, ﴿and were harmed in My way﴾ by what they suffered from the deniers. It is related from some of the gnostics that if a people have not tasted the bitterness of the harm of the deniers, they will not attain the sweetness of the cup of nearness to Allah, Exalted. For this reason al-Junayd, may his secret be sanctified, said: "May Allah, Exalted, reward our brothers on our behalf with good. They drove us, by their harshness, back to Allah, Exalted, and they fought their own souls for My sake, though the soul is their greatest enemy, and they were slain by the sword of annihilation." ﴿I will surely remove from them their evil deeds﴾, the minor and major sins from the remnants of their attributes and their essences. ﴿And I will surely admit them into gardens﴾, three in number, namely the garden of actions, the garden of attributes, and the garden of the Essence, ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾, the rivers of knowledge and manifestations, ﴿as a reward from Allah﴾, who comprises all attributes, ﴿and with Allah is the best reward﴾, so no reward is in the hand of anyone else at all.

﴿Let not the movement of those who disbelieve through the lands deceive you﴾, that is, those veiled from the oneness, ﴿in the worldly stations and states﴾, ﴿is a little enjoyment﴾, because of the swiftness of its passing and the uselessness of its benefit, ﴿then their refuge is Hell﴾, which is deprivation, ﴿and wretched is the resting place﴾ which they chose according to their readiness.

*(End of part 1 of 2)*

[Page 178]

Commentary of al-Alusi (*Ruh al-Ma'ani*) on surah 3, verse 200 (part 2 of 2):

﴿But those who fear their Lord, for them are gardens﴾, by stripping themselves of the utmost stripping (*tajarrud*), ﴿three﴾ in exchange for that, ﴿as a welcome gift from Allah﴾, prepared for them. ﴿And what is with Allah﴾ of the blessings of witnessing, the subtle favours of nearness, and the sweetness of union ﴿is better for the righteous﴾. ﴿Among the People of the Book are those who believe in Allah﴾, and realize the essential Oneness (*al-tawhid al-dhati*). ﴿And in what has been revealed to you﴾, of the knowledge of Oneness and uprightness, ﴿and in what has been revealed to them﴾, of the knowledge of the origin and the return, and attaining the degrees. ﴿Humbly submitting to Allah﴾, before the essential manifestation, for nothing is manifested by Allah, the Exalted, except that it submits to Him. ﴿They do not sell the signs of Allah﴾, the Exalted, which are the manifestations of His attributes, ﴿for a small price﴾. ﴿Those, for them is their reward with their Lord﴾, which is those gardens. ﴿Indeed Allah is swift in reckoning﴾, so He delivers their reward to them without delay.

﴿O you who believe, be patient﴾ against sins, ﴿and endure﴾ in acts of obedience, ﴿and stand firm﴾, binding the spirits through witnessing, ﴿and fear Allah﴾ from witnessing others (*aghyar*), ﴿so that you may prosper﴾ by being stripped of your cares and passing thoughts. Or: ﴿be patient﴾ in the station of the self (*nafs*) through striving (*mujahadah*), ﴿and endure﴾ in the station of the heart (*qalb*) together with the manifestations, ﴿and stand firm﴾ in the station of the spirit (*ruh*), your essences, lest lassitude or heedlessness overtake you, and ﴿fear Allah﴾ from opposition, turning away and harshness, ﴿so that you may succeed﴾ with true prosperity. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to grant us the fullest share of complying with these commands and what follows from them, by His bounty and generosity.

These ten verses were what the Prophet (ﷺ) used to recite every night, as Ibn al-Sunni, Abu Nu'aym and Ibn 'Asakir narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.

al-Darimi narrated from 'Uthman, who said: "Whoever recites the end of Al 'Imran in a night, Allah records for him the standing (in prayer) of a night." al-Tabarani narrated from the report of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ): "Whoever recites the surah in which Al 'Imran is mentioned on Friday, Allah and His angels will send blessings upon him until the sun sets." The report "Whoever recites Surat Al 'Imran will be given security for each verse on the bridge of Hell" is fabricated (*mawdu'*, forged) and invented against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Scholars have criticized those exegetes who cited it. We ask Allah, the Exalted, to preserve us from error and to protect us from mistake and nonsense; indeed He is Generous, Kind, Compassionate and Merciful. Let this be the conclusion of what I dictated of the tafsir (exegesis) of al-Fatihah and the two Zahrawan (the two luminous surahs). I earnestly ask Allah, the Exalted, with sincerity, to bring me to the tafsir of the two protective surahs (al-Mu'awwidhatayn). This is the first volume of *Ruh al-Ma'ani*, and, if Allah wills, the second volume will follow. Its completion was on the first day of the sacred month of Muharram in the year 1254 AH. May Allah bless and grant peace to our master Muhammad, and to his family and all his companions. Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds. Amin.
